edits.old: SERVER-130149 proposes letting a running build adopt increased maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes after a spill boundary. The ticket describes a current runtime-adoption gap and had no fix version on its October 22 update; the proposal does not authorize changes to Atlas tier-fixed settings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)
edits.new: SERVER-130149 proposes letting a running index build re-read and apply an increased maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes after a spill boundary. The ticket describes a current gap: changing the value at runtime does not help a build already trapped in a bad spill pattern. It is unresolved with Fix Version/s None, and the page was last updated Oct 26 2026. Separately, the MongoDB manual says that on Atlas the default values vary by cluster tier and maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes cannot be modified; the ticket does not mention Atlas. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-130149 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/core/index-creation/

evidence.quote: If maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes is increased while an index build is already running, the running build should re-read and apply the new value after a spill boundary.
The current gap is that changing maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes at runtime does not help enough once a running build is already trapped in this pattern.
On MongoDB Atlas, the default values of maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes and maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds vary by cluster tier. You cannot modify maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes on MongoDB Atlas.

edits.old: OneUptime's generic advice to change maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds through setParameter must be scoped to deployments that permit configuration; MongoDB's Atlas restriction rules out assuming that recipe applies there. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
edits.new: On MongoDB Atlas, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds uses cluster-tier default values that cannot be changed, so a recipe that changes it through setParameter (which works at runtime or startup on self-managed deployments) must not be assumed to apply on Atlas. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/reference/parameters/
